# Few-Shot Academy

> A free, open-source, local-first curriculum for generative AI, LLMs, vector databases, RAG,
> agents, and the Model Context Protocol. It is written for learners with no prior AI or
> computer science background and includes runnable labs.

Use the learning tracks in order: Foundations, Intermediate, then Advanced. The MCP track stands
alone. Advanced Concepts is a production cookbook. The blog contains sourced industry analysis,
not curriculum recaps.

## Start Here

- [Few-Shot Academy](https://fewshotacademy.com/): Choose a learning track or explore AI career paths.
- [Curriculum introduction](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/intro): What the curriculum covers, who it is for, and how to use it.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/fewshot-works/academy): Source for the site and runnable labs.

## Foundations

- [Overview](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/foundations/overview): The path from basic AI concepts to a local RAG capstone.
- [Chapter 0: Set Up Your Machine](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/foundations/setup): Install uv, VS Code, and Ollama for the labs.
- [Chapter 1: What Is AI, Really?](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/foundations/what-is-ai): How AI, machine learning, deep learning, and generative AI relate.
- [Chapter 2: What Is a Large Language Model?](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/foundations/what-is-an-llm): How LLMs predict text one token at a time.
- [Bonus: Using AI Responsibly](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/foundations/02b-responsible-ai-use): Privacy, bias, verification, and intellectual-property basics.
- [Chapter 3: Prompting 101](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/foundations/prompting-101): Zero-shot, few-shot, and system prompts with a runnable comparison.
- [Chapter 4: What Is an Embedding?](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/foundations/what-is-an-embedding): How text becomes vectors that preserve semantic similarity.
- [Chapter 5: What Is a Vector Database?](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/foundations/what-is-a-vector-database): Storing and searching embeddings efficiently.
- [Chapter 6: What Is RAG?](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/foundations/what-is-rag): Turning an LLM into an open-book answerer.
- [Chapter 7: What Is an AI Agent?](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/foundations/what-is-an-ai-agent): How agents choose actions and call tools.
- [Chapter 8: Q&A Bot Capstone](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/foundations/capstone-qa-bot): Build a RAG bot over your own documents.

## Intermediate

- [Overview](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/intermediate/overview): Retrieval, prompting, tools, agents, memory, evaluation, and a capstone.
- [Chapter 1: Chunking Strategies](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/intermediate/chunking-strategies): Compare fixed-size, recursive, and semantic chunking.
- [Chapter 2: Choosing an Embedding Model](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/intermediate/choosing-embedding-model): Compare quality, latency, and cost.
- [Chapter 3: Better Retrieval](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/intermediate/better-retrieval): Metadata filtering, hybrid search, and re-ranking.
- [Chapter 4: Prompt Patterns](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/intermediate/prompt-patterns): Reasoning, structured output, and function calling.
- [Chapter 5: Tool Use](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/intermediate/tool-use): Build a tool-calling loop by hand.
- [Chapter 6: Your First Agent](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/intermediate/your-first-agent): Rebuild the loop with LangChain and examine the abstraction.
- [Chapter 7: Memory](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/intermediate/memory): Short-term checkpoints and summarized long-term memory.
- [Chapter 8: Evaluating What You Built](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/intermediate/evaluating): Measure retrieval and generated answers.
- [Chapter 9: Multi-Tool Agent Capstone](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/intermediate/capstone): Combine calculation, search, RAG, and memory.

## Advanced

- [Overview](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced/overview): Production patterns for agentic RAG systems.
- [Chapter 1: Multi-Agent Patterns](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced/multi-agent-patterns): Supervisor, hierarchy, and swarm patterns.
- [Chapter 2: Advanced RAG](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced/advanced-rag): Query rewriting, HyDE, multi-hop retrieval, and self-correction.
- [Chapter 3: Fine-Tuning vs. RAG vs. Prompting](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced/fine-tuning-vs-rag-vs-prompting): Choose an adaptation strategy and run a small LoRA comparison.
- [Chapter 4: Guardrails and Safety](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced/guardrails-and-safety): Input checks, output validation, and their limits.
- [Chapter 5: Observability](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced/observability): Trace model calls with OpenTelemetry.
- [Chapter 6: Production Concerns](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced/production-concerns): Caching, rate limiting, and streaming.
- [Chapter 7: Shipping It](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced/shipping-it): Package an agent with FastAPI and Docker.
- [Chapter 8: Evaluated Agent Capstone](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced/capstone): Add guardrails, tracing, and evaluation to an agent.

## Model Context Protocol

- [MCP track overview](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/mcp/overview): The standalone track and its final system.
- [Chapter 1: What Is MCP?](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/mcp/what-is-mcp): Host, client, and server architecture.
- [Chapter 2: Build an MCP Server](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/mcp/building-your-own-mcp-server): Wrap a Python tool with the official SDK.
- [Chapter 3: One Agent, Many Servers](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/mcp/one-agent-many-servers): Connect an agent to multiple MCP servers.
- [Chapter 4: Transports and Deployment](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/mcp/transports-and-deployment): Compare stdio and HTTP deployment.
- [Chapter 5: Resources, Prompts, and Sampling](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/mcp/resources-prompts-sampling): Explore MCP primitives beyond tools.
- [Chapter 6: MCP Security](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/mcp/mcp-security): Defend against malicious tool descriptions and output.
- [Chapter 7: Agent2Agent](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/mcp/a2a): Discover and delegate to a remote agent with A2A.
- [Chapter 8: MCP Capstone](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/mcp/capstone): Combine servers, a domain guard, memory, and a Streamlit UI.

## Advanced Concepts

- [Overview](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced-concepts/overview): Standalone production topics that can be read in any order.
- [Prompt Engineering](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced-concepts/prompt-engineering): Structure, grounding, chaining, ReAct, self-refine, and optimization.
- [Token and Cost Management](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced-concepts/token-cost-management): Context trimming, prompt caching, model selection, and batching.
- [Agent Security](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced-concepts/agent-security): Stop indirect prompt injection with tool-call policy.
- [Human in the Loop](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced-concepts/human-in-the-loop): Pause tool calls for approve, edit, reject, or respond decisions.
- [Role-Based Access Control](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced-concepts/rbac): Scope tool permissions and limits by role.
- [Chaos Engineering](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced-concepts/chaos-engineering): Inject tool faults and measure agent degradation.
- [Continuous Adversarial Evaluation](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced-concepts/continuous-adversarial-evaluation): Test defenses against varied attacks and secure the eval harness.
- [AI Gateways](https://fewshotacademy.com/docs/advanced-concepts/ai-gateways): Build a provider boundary and deliberate failover policy.

## Career and Interview Preparation

- [Career tracks](https://fewshotacademy.com/career-tracks): Compare five roles that build, operate, sell, or manage AI systems.
- [Forward-Deployed Engineer](https://fewshotacademy.com/career-tracks/forward-deployed-engineer): Work with customers to turn ambiguous problems into production systems.
- [Applied and Agentic AI Engineer](https://fewshotacademy.com/career-tracks/applied-agentic-ai-engineer): Build and ship RAG pipelines and tool-using agents.
- [AI Product Manager](https://fewshotacademy.com/career-tracks/ai-product-manager): Define and guide AI products.
- [SRE and Reliability Engineer for AI Agents](https://fewshotacademy.com/career-tracks/sre-reliability-engineer): Operate agents against reliability, cost, and latency goals.
- [AI Solutions Architect and Presales](https://fewshotacademy.com/career-tracks/ai-solutions-architect-presales): Lead discovery, prototypes, demos, and technical proposals.
- [Interview preparation](https://fewshotacademy.com/interview-prep): Choose a role and prepare for its interview loop.
- [Technical rounds](https://fewshotacademy.com/interview-prep/technical-round): Role-specific technical questions and exercises.
- [Behavioral rounds](https://fewshotacademy.com/interview-prep/behavioral-round): Role-specific prompts and answer frameworks.
- [Case studies](https://fewshotacademy.com/interview-prep/case-studies): Practice role-specific take-home and live cases.

## Blog

- [Blog index](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog): Sourced analysis of AI releases, incidents, security, regulation, and engineering practice.
- [GPT-6 Astra: the harness is the product](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/gpt-6-astra-the-harness-is-the-product): Why Astra's AGI claim depends on persistent context, searchable history, async tools, and mid-turn steering.
- [Stop calling LLM APIs directly](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/stop-calling-llm-apis-directly): Why model fallback needs an application-owned boundary and tested policy.
- [MCP is done pretending agents are people](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/mcp-roadmap-agent-identity): What the MCP roadmap means for agent identity and delegation.
- [MCP just went stateless](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/mcp-goes-stateless): Production implications of the July 2026 MCP specification revision.
- [Frontier models don't make safer agents](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/frontier-models-arent-safer-agents): What adversarial tool environments reveal about agent security.
- [Managed AI platforms trade one lock-in for another](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/managed-ai-platforms-lock-in): Compare cloud AI platforms with direct provider APIs.
- [OWASP checked its LLM Top 10 against real incidents](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/owasp-llm-top-10-2026): How incident data changed the 2026 ranking.
- [A new toolkit unifies three ways to catch a hallucination](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/sirin-hallucination-detection-toolkit): Compare three hallucination-detection methods with SIRIN.
- [OpenAI's cyber-hunting model found a Chrome vulnerability](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/openai-cyber-model-chrome-vulnerability): What GPT-5.6-Cyber demonstrated and what its autonomy limits mean.
- [Every major AI lab shipped an agent model this week](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/open-weight-models-agent-benchmarks): Compare agentic benchmarks across three model releases.
- [NVIDIA shows KV caches can move between model sizes](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/cross-model-kv-cache-transfer): Reuse prompt-processing work across related models.
- [What the rogue-agent headlines got wrong](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/rogue-agent-incidents-guardrails): Separate real security incidents from misleading framing.
- [OWASP published a security top 10 for MCP](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/owasp-mcp-top-10): Review all ten MCP risk categories and examples.
- [The EU AI Act deadline moved](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/eu-ai-act-obligations): What changed and what high-risk obligations still require.
- [Agent memory became its own product category](https://fewshotacademy.com/blog/agent-memory-first-class): Compare agent-memory frameworks, benchmarks, and open problems.
